description: Fake bank support plus remote access. The caller talked the customer into installing a screen-sharing app and reading out an OTP. This is the clearest-cut case in the cohort and the one where speed matters most - by the time a human reviews it, the attacker may already be inside the session.

customer.normal_activity: Pension credits, domestic transfers under 1500 USD, branch-assisted banking.

signals.redacted_quote: install the support app so I can see your screen and fix it
read me the six digits so I can cancel the charge

evidence.claim: Caller impersonating the fraud department directed the customer to install screen-sharing software and read out a one-time passcode
evidence.redacted_quote: install the support app so I can see your screen and fix it

evidence.claim: 22000 USD to a first-seen international beneficiary from an account whose largest prior transfer was 1500 USD
Published advisory: no legitimate bank ever asks a customer to install remote-access software or disclose a one-time passcode

demo_note: Tests the critical-evidence path specifically. remote_access_request and otp_request are the two labels marked critical in fusion, which means this escalates on evidence alone - it would still reach a human even if the risk score came back at zero. Worth demonstrating by dropping the risk score to 0 live and showing the action does not change.
